context: Crossfilter dashboard with 3 linked histograms (departure hour, delay minutes, distance miles) over 2000 synthetic flights; brushing any histogram filters the others in real time via crossfilter semantics
first_impression: Exceptionally clean and uncluttered — three stacked histograms share a single blue hue and ghost-bar encoding that makes the filter state instantly legible.
what_works: Ghost bars (gray total, blue filtered) are the ideal encoding for crossfilter — the viewer sees both the full distribution and the filtered subset in one glance without needing a legend. Animation is well-managed: no transitions during drag for responsiveness, 250ms ease on brush-end to show state change without distraction.
what_doesnt: The delay histogram's heavy right skew compresses the interesting long-delay tail into the rightmost ~20% of the axis, making precise brushing in that region fiddly. Perceptual evaluation of brush-drag responsiveness and transition smoothness is limited without seeing it in motion.
